name: Create an accessible dark hero block pattern
query: Create a bold full-width hero block pattern for a creative agency theme. Use a dark background, a large heading, a short subtitle, and two CTA buttons. It should be available from the inserter.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Route the task to wp-patterns after classifying the repository and pattern target
Step 2: Confirm or infer the theme slug, text domain, pattern title, slug, and category
Step 3: Create a filesystem pattern file under patterns/
Step 4: Add required PHP headers including Title, Slug, and Categories, plus useful Keywords and Viewport Width
Step 5: Use valid block markup with balanced block comments and valid JSON attributes
Step 6: Use theme presets for dark background, text color, spacing, typography, and button styling instead of inline CSS or custom classes
Step 7: Escape and internationalize all visible strings and attribute text with the target text domain
Step 8: Keep heading levels accessible, use descriptive CTA labels, and avoid scripts or query-time PHP
Step 9: Verify the pattern appears in the inserter and inserts without block validation errors
success_criteria: Pattern file is placed in patterns/ and uses a theme-scoped slug
PHP header includes Title, Slug, Categories, Keywords, and Viewport Width
Block markup is valid, balanced, and parses without recovery prompts
All user-visible strings use escaped i18n functions such as esc_html_e() or esc_html__()
Any URL or attribute output uses esc_url(), esc_attr_e(), or esc_attr__() as appropriate
Styling relies on theme presets and block attributes, not inline style tags, scripts, or custom CSS classes
Hero uses an accessible heading level, readable contrast, and descriptive CTA button text
Verification mentions checking the inserter and WordPress editor parsing
